- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer or adjust downward early.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5) after sharp spikes; apply lag correction or dampen initial forecast rise.
- After a true price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or trending sideways, model tends to drift toward mean; apply mean reversion heuristic: forecast = prior 7-day average ± 2σ.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in low-sentiment periods; increase forecast variance or add stochastic noise for low-sentiment windows.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 0.0–0.4), model often fails to anticipate sharp reversals; add early warning rule: if sentiment drops below 0.3 for 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days.
